From: Tom Ellis <finance@aurorahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Health Accounts <accounts@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Gross-to-Net reconciliation for multi-entity subaccounts

Hi Rachel —

We began preparing for next quarter's invoicing and ran into a gap: Aurora bills centrally but needs the vendor invoices apportioned across three legal entities (Aurora US, Aurora EU, Aurora Labs) and our tax team requires gross-to-net reconciliation lines so VAT can be reclaimed appropriately per entity.

Current constraints:
- Redwood invoices arrive as a single customer-level bill grouped by customer master ID.
- Our AP team needs a line-level mapping back to our internal subaccount IDs, GL codes, and VAT IDs.
- We also need a clear path for credit notes when seats move between entities mid-cycle.

Can Redwood provide a recommended handoff format and a playbook for:
1) producing split invoice lines that show gross charges per subaccount, VAT per line, and net amounts;
2) a remittance/collector file to support reconciliation for our treasury;
3) example of credit note flows for mid-period reallocations.

Happy to jump on a short call if helpful — we'd like to get this in place before the Sept billing run.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Director, Finance Operations
Aurora Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Gross-to-Net reconciliation for multi-entity subaccounts

Tom —

Thanks for the clear note. We can support a gross-to-net split across subaccounts; below is a recommended lightweight approach we use for similar customers. I've attached a mapping template and our VAT guidance PDF.

High-level proposal (steps):
1) Invoice emission: Redwood will continue to issue a single PDF invoice per billing cycle, but the invoice line-item CSV (attached) will include explicit fields: original_line_id, subaccount_id, legal_entity, gl_code, gross_amount, vat_rate, vat_amount, net_amount, customer_reference.

2) Remittance/collector file: we can produce a per-cycle CSV called "collector_remit_<cycle>.csv" that aggregates by collector (your treasury) and lists which entity each payment should be applied to. This file includes payment_due_date, invoice_number, line_id, remit_entity_tax_id.

3) Credit flows: when seats are reallocated mid-cycle we create a credit_note with references to original_line_id and new_line_id. Credit notes appear as separate rows in the line-level CSV with negative gross/net and a required reason_code.

Ask from your side: please populate the attached mapping template with the subaccount_id and preferred GL mapping so we can draft a sample August cycle output. Also confirm which entity should be the primary collector when Aurora wants netting across entities (i.e., do you net across US/EU/Labs or do you want each billed independently?).

I'll loop in Ben to confirm GL and tax treatment on our side. Proposed timeline: mapping back from you by Fri 8/6, Redwood sample output by Tue 8/10, and SOW amendment signature if needed the week of 8/16.

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subaccount_mapping_template.csv (stub), vat_guidelines.pdf (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Gross-to-Net reconciliation for multi-entity subaccounts

Adding a couple of accounting notes from our side:

- GL/ERP mapping: we can include a gl_code column in the invoice export but final posting to your ERP will be driven by your AP rules. Recommend mapping file include both gl_code and department/cost_center.

- VAT handling: for EU entities we will emit VAT as line-level VAT_amount with the vat_rate explicit. If you prefer VAT on a separate summary row per legal entity we can provide that as an optional field.

- Credit notes: please decide whether credits should be issued as separate credit invoices (preferred) or as negative line items on the next invoice. Separate credit invoices are easier to reconcile for multi-entity posting.

- Audit field: we'll add invoice_line_origin to help trace generated charges back to subscription events (useful for tax audits).

Marissa — can you confirm whether a contractual amendment / SOW addendum is required for us to start shipping line-level CSVs and whether collections should hit a new collector_id for Aurora's netting preference?

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <finance@aurorahealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Gross-to-Net reconciliation for multi-entity subaccounts

Tom —

Thanks — this is all doable. Quick checklist and next actions so we have alignment:

1) Aurora to return redwood_subaccount_mapping_template.csv populated with: subaccount_id, legal_entity_tag (US/EU/LABS), primary_collector_id, preferred_gl_code, vat_id_per_entity. (Due: Fri 08/06 — if you missed that date, please send by EOD 08/12 so we don't slip September billing.)

2) Redwood will deliver a sample invoice CSV for the August cycle by Tue 08/10 showing: line_id, original_invoice_number, subaccount_id, gross, vat_rate, vat_amount, net, invoice_line_origin.

3) Credit note handling: by default we'll issue separate credit invoices referencing original_line_id. If Aurora prefers negative lines on next invoice, flag it in mapping.

4) Contracting: small SOW amendment required for per-line reporting and additional CSV retention (12 months). DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/some/dslink/ABC12345 (attached SOW). Please sign if ok.

5) Collections handoff: once mapping is final we'll create a collector_remit.csv scheduled to be dropped to your secure SFTP at remit.aurora/receipts. If you need the file pushed to a different endpoint let us know.

If you prefer a 30-minute call to walk your AP and tax folks through the sample, Rachel can set it up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
